data.title: Meta AI Chief Uses 167-Year-Old Riemann Problem to Argue Superintelligence Is Near
data.description: Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang argued Sunday that superintelligence is near, citing a proof of the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis developed at rival Anthropic. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he found the proof while working with Claude on November 20, and the Lean and Mathlib communities certified it the next day, according to BeInCrypto. Wang did not name the proof or Alpöge in his essay, describing the result as the work of an “alien mind”; Queen Mary University of London professor Abhishek Saha credited Alpöge and said others with similar AI access had not produced a proof. Wang argues AI systems may automate AI research but rejects the idea that artificial superintelligence is inevitable, saying society should resist handing control to AI. Meta, meanwhile, reported $34.91 billion in third-quarter capital expenditures and negative $2.12 billion in free cash flow, and expects full-year 2026 spending of $135 billion to $145 billion. It plans to shift Reality Labs investment toward AI and cut its losses next year, while creating a new class of stock partly to fund the buildout.

data.title: Ark Buys 164 Million Anthropic Shares Worth $145.9 Million
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Cathie Wood's Ark Invest bought 1.64 million Anthropic shares through its exchange-traded funds on November 20 and 21, for a total of $145.9 million. Anthropic listed on Nasdaq on November 19.

Last week, Ark also sold $5.8 million worth of 3iQ Solana Staking ETF shares, nearly $9 million worth of 3iQ Ether Staking ETF shares, $1.84 million worth of Bullish shares and $1.48 million worth of Robinhood shares. It bought $24.7 million worth of Block shares.

data.title: Shoprite Takes Stake in DN Invest as It and Investec Deepen Mobile Bets
data.description: Shoprite Holdings Ltd. and Investec are deepening their bets on fintech and mobile services as Shoprite buys a stake in DN Invest Ltd., a technology, hardware and financing firm, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: STOCKS | Dan Bin Responds to Questions Over Dongfang Harbor’s Risk Controls After Nvidia’s 14% Drop
data.description: According to Jin10, Nvidia fell more than 14% on November 20, while the chipmaker was Dongfang Harbor’s overseas funds’ second-largest holding at the end of the third quarter; the funds also significantly increased their position in Nvidia during the quarter. Critics questioned whether Dongfang Harbor had overlooked the rate-hike cycle, geopolitical wars and pressure on AI valuations, and raised concerns about its risk controls. Founder Dan Bin said the firm did not initiate a major position reduction because it remained optimistic about the broader AI-era trend, and that AI applications account for 60% of its current holdings.

data.title: Samsung Securities Confirms Personal Data Leak Affecting 8,241 Customers
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Yonhap News Agency, Samsung Securities said it discovered unauthorized access to its customer feedback system on Saturday. The company confirmed that personal information belonging to 8,241 customers was exposed; data in attachments uploaded to the system included names, account numbers, addresses, contact details and driver’s license numbers, among 13 categories that varied by customer. The intrusion occurred on November 21, and customers who had not used the system were not affected. Samsung Securities said no customer information outside the affected system was exposed. It blocked the relevant IP addresses, suspended related services and notified South Korea’s Financial Supervisory Service and Korea Internet & Security Agency. The company said it would contact affected customers individually and strengthen its security systems.

data.title: Citi: Short-Term Strategy Shifts to Buying Dips as Markets May Need Days to Bottom
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Citi said in its November 21 market commentary that markets are at a key turning point, marking a shift from its previously bearish stance. In the short term, the bank is moving from selling rallies to buying dips, though trading could remain volatile over the coming weeks.

Citi said the sell-off coincided with gamma positioning reaching a record high, and the expiration of some positions could help stabilize markets. Whether a V-shaped rebound will occur remains unclear, and markets may need several days to form a bottom. The bank recommended rolling put options to lower strike prices, covering short positions, and buying stocks and federal funds futures. It plans to further review and refine the shift over the weekend.

Citi said the AI bubble has burst and a market washout appears to be underway, urging investors to look beyond hype and bubbles for quality and value. The bank expects the shift to have ripple effects across global markets, with the S&P 500 nearing a turning point while other markets may have further room to fall.

data.title: Bernstein: High Memory Chip Prices May Weigh on Consumer Electronics Shipments
data.description: According to Jin10, Bernstein analysts said in a research report that high memory chip prices may continue to weigh on consumer electronics shipments into next year. They estimated that global smartphone shipments could fall 14% this year and 5% in 2027. Memory chip price increases are expected to ease in the second half of next year, but high smartphone prices could delay a demand recovery until 2028. Global PC shipments could decline by a low double-digit percentage this year and 6% in 2027. Meanwhile, demand for AI devices such as smart glasses may accelerate, driven by new Ray-Ban Meta products and AI glasses from Samsung and other brands. Rising memory chip prices pose challenges for consumer electronics sellers, but Apple’s position remains unmatched, with its shares of the smartphone and PC markets continuing to rise.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | COMEX Silver Registered Stocks Hold Steady; 341,000-Ounce Net Outflow Hits Eligible
data.description: According to Jin10, COMEX silver Registered stocks were unchanged, while Eligible stocks recorded a net outflow of 341,000 ounces in one day. Asahi and JPMorgan withdrew a combined 890,100 ounces, and cumulative November SI deliveries reached 2,063 contracts.

data.title: Yole Group: AI and EVs Reshape Power Management Chip Market, Driving Double-Digit Growth
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Yole Group expects the power management integrated circuit (PMIC) market, once centered on smartphones and home appliances, to be reshaped around AI infrastructure and sustain double-digit growth. The global market is forecast to expand from $38.5 billion in 2025 to about $68 billion in 2031, an average annual growth rate of 10%. PMICs regulate voltage and current inside electronic devices to provide power efficiently, and their applications are expanding into AI data centers and electric vehicles.

Communications and infrastructure, including AI data centers, are the main growth drivers. Yole Group forecasts that this segment will grow from $6.4 billion in 2025 to about $18 billion in 2031, at an average annual rate of 19%, accounting for about 40% of the overall PMIC market’s increase. As AI chips become more powerful, demand for power-management chips is also rising. Power consumption per GPU rack has increased from about 40 kilowatts to 250 kilowatts and is expected to reach 600 kilowatts to 1 megawatt in the next few years.

Yole Group said capacity expansion is limited relative to demand growth and that BCD (bipolar-CMOS-DMOS) processes used to manufacture PMICs face a structural supply shortage. The process integrates analog circuits, digital control circuits and high-voltage power devices on a single chip. Global PMIC wafer output, measured in 8-inch equivalents, is forecast to rise from about 45 million wafers annually to 56 million by 2031. Although the share of 12-inch BCD production lines is increasing, the industry generally expects large-scale capacity to emerge only in 2028–2030. South Korea’s DB HiTek and SK Key Foundry, whose main production processes are 8-inch, are foundry manufacturers of BCD-based power semiconductors.

The automotive and mobility market is forecast to reach $18.3 billion in 2031, driven mainly by electric vehicles’ shift from 400-volt to 800-volt platforms, which nearly doubles the value of battery-monitoring chips in each vehicle. Industrial PMICs are expected to exceed $16 billion in 2031, with adoption in industry, logistics and humanoid robotics contributing to growth. Consumer electronics and mobile devices are mature markets, growing at an average annual rate of just 2.3%. Siran Zhu, a market researcher in Yole Group’s power electronics division, said AI infrastructure, electric vehicles and, over the longer term, robotics are making the PMIC market more diverse and technology-intensive.

data.title: dtcpay Becomes Pilot Partner for Visa’s First Stablecoin Funds Transfer Project in Asia-Pacific
data.description: dtcpay has become a pilot partner for Visa’s first stablecoin-driven funds transfer project in Asia-Pacific. According to Odaily, dtcpay, which holds a major payment institution license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, will use USDC to pre-fund cross-border payments, with recipients receiving funds in fiat currency. The service allows businesses with cross-border payment needs, including platforms, remittance providers, e-commerce marketplaces and payroll providers, to send payments to bank accounts, Visa cards and digital wallets. Visa Direct is a real-time funds transfer platform that connects more than 18 billion endpoints.

data.title: Galxe Sets January 15, 2027, Deadline for Unclaimed Token Reward Refunds
data.description:
Galxe says project teams must apply for refunds of unclaimed token rewards by January 15, 2027. According to Foresight News, the Web3 growth platform is working with partners to wind down existing campaigns and settle outstanding balances as its services are gradually shut down. Refund applications for Business+ subscriptions and Space deposits must be submitted by December 5. Teams with completed Earndrop projects can withdraw unclaimed tokens directly from smart contracts, while ongoing Earndrops will continue according to their original unlock schedules.

Foresight News previously reported that Galxe was integrating its team and brand into Gravity. Galxe Quest, Galxe ID, Galxe Passport, and related services are set to close gradually. Campaign participation ends on December 5, reward claims close on December 15, and the website will then switch to read-only mode.

data.title: Grvt Burns 900,000 GRVT in Second Buyback, Total Burn Reaches 2 Million
data.description: Grvt completed its second buyback and burn, removing 900,000 GRVT and bringing the cumulative amount burned to 2 million tokens. According to Foresight News, the CeDeFi platform announced the burn in a post.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | China Sentences Official to Death for Foreign Spying
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China said it sentenced an official to death for spying for a foreign intelligence service and publicized the case as a warning against leaking state secrets.

data.title: UK Pension Fund Managers Say They Were Fired for Underweighting U.S. Tech Stocks
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has received complaints from fund managers who said pension trustees fired them for investing too little in U.S. technology stocks and missing out on high returns. Trustees can appoint or dismiss asset managers overseeing retirees’ money, and dismissals of managers who reduced large technology-stock holdings in favor of diversified strategies have increased in recent years, a person familiar with the matter said.

U.S. technology stocks have surged in recent years amid the artificial intelligence boom, though markets have been volatile in recent weeks. Anthropic completed one of the largest initial public offerings on record last week, while the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 entered bear-market territory.

The FCA plans to remind pension-scheme trustees that they should not assess fund managers solely on investment returns. Other measures, including the risk of excessive portfolio concentration in a small number of stocks, should also be considered. The regulator said performance assessments often cannot rely on a single measure and that schemes should seek long-term value for savers by considering managers’ stated objectives and investment styles.

A person familiar with the plans cited a similar situation before the dot-com crash in 2000, when some lower-risk managers were dismissed after reducing technology holdings and diversifying. Some asset managers have complained that trustees dismissed them despite their arguments that reducing technology exposure helped control risk.

The FCA requires managers to assess their funds’ value annually, considering performance as well as service quality and fees. It last reviewed the relevant rules in 2023. The U.K. Department for Work and Pensions said this July that it planned to address performance differences among workplace pension schemes; data showed a 55% return gap between the best- and worst-performing schemes over five years. The FCA and The Pensions Regulator consulted earlier this year on how schemes should measure and compare investment value, with new rules and guidance expected in 2027.

David Fogarty, a senior trustee director at Dalriada Trustees, said artificial intelligence’s effects extend beyond technology stocks, requiring trustees to engage with asset managers more broadly. He added that investment decisions should consider potential returns, risks and costs.

data.title: Zhipu Releases GLM-5.4 Model on Coding Plan
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Jin10, an official operator at AI company Zhipu said GLM-5.4 is now available on Coding Plan, with new visual capabilities and stronger general coding capabilities. Over the past three months, the company advanced both Scaling Loop and model scale; users first saw changes brought by Loop Transformer. Quotas for V2, V3, and Team users have increased to 1.5 times. Users can access the model by setting its name to glm-5.4.

data.title: STOCKS | BHP Plans to Double South Australian Copper Output to 650,000 Tonnes Before 2040; Shares Rise 2.3%
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, BHP, the world’s largest publicly listed copper producer, announced on November 23 that it plans to double annual output from its South Australian copper operations to 650,000 tonnes before 2040. BHP’s Australian-listed shares rose about 2.3% to 52.6 Australian dollars as of publication.

BHP plans to increase its group-attributable annual copper production to 2 million tonnes by 2035, from about 1.4 million tonnes currently, an increase of about 43%. Its South Australian copper operations are expected to account for about one-third of the group’s planned additional copper output through 2035. The expansion will proceed in two phases: first raising annual output to about 500,000 tonnes, then to 650,000 tonnes before 2040.

BHP said the expansion will be funded mainly by operating cash flow from its copper business, which it expects to generate about $35 billion in cumulative attributable free cash flow by 2035. The company said long-term copper demand will be supported by electrification, renewable energy investment, digital transformation, and AI infrastructure. It also warned that existing copper mines cannot supply enough to meet future demand and that the global copper industry needs more investment and new capacity to address the long-term supply-demand gap.

data.title: Malaysia Palm Oil Industry Says CPO Tax-Waiver Opportunity Is Over
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Malaysia’s palm oil industry says the period when waiving the crude palm oil (CPO) export tax could have boosted shipments and eased stockpile accumulation has passed.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Maintains Fed Rate-Hike Forecast After 100-Basis-Point Tightening
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Chaoxiang Research, Goldman Sachs U.S. economist David Mericle said the bank’s U.S. Financial Conditions Index has tightened by about 100 basis points since early September, including more than 40 basis points last week. The move was driven mainly by lower U.S. equity valuations, rising 10-year Treasury yields and a stronger dollar. If conditions remain at current levels, Goldman estimates they would reduce U.S. year-over-year GDP growth in the fourth quarter of 2027 by 0.5 percentage points.

Goldman expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates by 25 basis points in December and by another 25 basis points in March 2027, despite market-driven tightening approaching the equivalent of a 100-basis-point rate increase. The bank cited elevated inflation and economic growth above its potential rate. Further market selloffs driven by concerns about declining AI capital spending could substitute for next year’s rate hike.

data.title: AI Data Center Boom Drives Billions Into Private Infrastructure
data.description: According to CNBC, infrastructure fundraising rebounded in the third quarter of 2026, with $62 billion raised across 21 funds, bringing the year’s total to $101 billion across 65 funds. Brookfield Asset Management raised roughly $50 billion in infrastructure commitments over the past year, including $26 billion for the latest vintage of its flagship strategy. The firm said $13 billion of that amount came after the quarter ended and that it was on track to exceed its $30 billion target in early 2027. Data centers, communications networks, renewables and energy storage have accounted for a growing share of infrastructure investment as AI expands. Goldman Sachs’ 2026 Global Alternatives Survey found that 43% of institutional investors had a more favorable outlook on infrastructure than a year earlier, while 49% of investors with a target allocation to the sector said they were under-allocated.

data.title: Shopify CEO Says Allegations Surrounding Jensen Huang’s Departure “Seemed Orchestrated”
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke said on David Senra’s podcast that the timing of allegations surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure “seemed orchestrated” and resembled a carefully planned effort to oust him. The allegations included an affair and an investigation potentially involving foreign intelligence operations. Lütke acknowledged he could be wrong and that Huang may have had an affair.

Lütke said some people could benefit from Huang’s departure but did not identify anyone. He called Nvidia board members “fools” and said their rushed decisions during the scandal risked turning the company into a traditional corporation. Nvidia previously said Huang voluntarily resigned because his disclosed conduct did not meet the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms. Lütke said the bar for finding Huang unfit to lead should be higher.
